items.title: Cascadu interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: He toured with Hamiet Bluiett and all these guys and everything, and I’m sitting there with the guy. I don’t know him, I don’t know anything about him, I just know that I saw you in my dream

ctx.x: I’m not sure if I can phrase this question correctly but if you had this spiritual calling, would there have been another way to pursue that call without being a percussionist? In order words could you have become a priest within that religion as opposed to following the percussion path?

I am sure. I’m sure there are people who have done it. But for me and for everybody the path is different. Right? For me it really happened in my relationship with the drum. So, and interestingly the drum that I was hearing, which I didn’t know, was batá. And I remember specifically when I went to, when I left Trinidad I went straight to Emile Latimer in Buffalo. Emile had set up a room in his house for me, I mean decorated with Africanisms all around. Listen, I came to Emile, I stayed with Emile for a month…

he was leading a drum circle, whether he had a gig that night at the club, etcetera. I was attached to Emile’s drums. Drum in tow and we went. And I left there a month later after I had had a vision and a dream that there was this entire, this entire lineage of drummers that I was supposed to come into contact with on my path. And I saw them all, Monk, I saw every single one of them in the dream, who I would have to connect with. And I told Emile, I got up and I told Emile about the dream. And Emile said,…
